newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: French sailor safe, hopes rise for Briton.
newsitem.headline: French sailor safe, hopes rise for Briton.

text.p: A French solo yachtsman was winched from a life raft in freezing waters near Antarctica on Thursday as hopes rose for the rescue of a British sailor and a third competitor in the same high-risk race lost radio contact.
Frenchman Thierry Dubois, stranded in a life raft in the Southern Ocean since Monday, was pulled to safety by an Australian navy helicopter at first light over the ocean.
An Australian defence force spokesman said Dubois was in good health despite his five-day ordeal.
Shortly before, tapping was heard from within the upturned yacht of missing Briton Tony Bullimore -- giving exhausted rescuers a boost.
Tony Bullimore, 56, is competing in the same Vendee Globe round-the-world race as Dubois.
"Spirits are lifting here. It could be two out of two," David Gray, spokesman for the Australian Marine Safety Authority, told Reuters.

In Paris, organisers of the race said they had lost contact with a third solo yachtsman, Canadian Gerry Roufs. Frenchwoman Isabelle Autissier, rescued in Australian waters two years ago, had agreed to turn back and look for him.
Australian officials said they had asked shipping in the area to look out for the Canadian but said he was thought to be in Chilean territorial waters.
Navy rescuers have been unable to determine whether Bullimore, who capsized on Sunday about 60 miles (100 km) from where Dubois overturned, was still alive in his upturned yacht.
But the crew of an Orion rescue plane circling over his yacht dropped a listening device into the water on Thursday and reported hearing tapping sounds from inside the yacht's hull.
An Australian navy frigate with Dubois on board was heading toward Bullimore's yacht and oil tanker Sanko Phoenix, en route from Cape Town to Sydney, diverted to the rescue site.
Gray said an attempt might even be made to lift Bullimore's yacht from the water onto the tanker with navy divers' help.
Defence Force spokesman Reynolds said the tapping sounds were picked up late on Wednesday.

"Now we hope this is Tony Bullimore tapping inside the yacht but we temper it by the fact that it could be some debris inside the yacht which has broken free and is tapping against the outside of the hull," he added.
Reynolds said a very weak signal had also been picked up from a small "personal locator beacon" carried by Bullimore.
Meanwhile Dubois, 29, was undergoing a precautionary medical examination on the frigate HMAS Adelaide after being picked up at 5.25 am (2125 GMT)
"Thierry Dubois is now on Australian soil," said Reynolds. "I am happy to report that he is well."
Dubois was found by a rescue plane on Monday clinging to the upturned hull of his yacht Pour Amnesty International and managed to scramble aboard a life raft.

The two yachtsmen were the latest competitors in the Vendee race to hit disaster south of Australia. Frenchman Rafael Dinelli, 28, arrived in Hobart, Tasmania, on Wednesday after he was rescued by a fellow competitor two days after Christmas.
The dramatic rescues of Dinelli and Dubois have been seen by some Australians as a chance to mend fences with Paris after last year's row over nuclear testing.

Australian sports minister Warwick Smith wrote to his French counterpart Guy Drut to say that while Australia was happy to comply with its international obligations to rescue the sailors, the race should be moved onto a more northerly and safer route.
